propositions: A model id containing a colon in its version suffix (e.g., 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0') is incorrectly treated as already provider-qualified, causing an explicitly configured provider to be silently discarded.

The current colon-based test for provider qualification cannot distinguish between a provider separator colon and a colon within a Bedrock model id's version suffix, resulting in wrong inference of the provider name from a fragment of the model id.

An explicitly configured provider must be checked and honoured before any scan of the model string, and conflicting provider directives (configured vs. inline qualifier) must raise LLMConfigError rather than silently picking a winner.

Two independent implementations of the same qualification test (in _resolve_target and infer_provider) can drift apart; both must route through a single shared function (split_provider_qualifier) with a regex-based identifier shape check.
